Lessons.Title: Exponential Functions with Base $e$
ExplanationParagraphs: Source-aligned goals: Comprehend that we can use $e^r$ as the growth factor of $f(t) = e^{rt}$ when we assume the rate $r$ is applied continuously. Interpret the parameters in the equations of exponential functions with the form $f(t)=P \boldcdot e^{rt}$.
A model P*e^(rt) has initial amount P and continuous growth rate r per time unit; its one-unit growth factor is e^r and its one-unit percent change is100(e^r-1). A negative r indicates decay.

When working on problems that involve \(e\), we often rely on calculators to estimate values. Find the \(e\) button on your calculator. Experiment with it to understand how it works. About how many bacteria were in the dish 10 hours after the scientist put the initial 50 bacteria in the dish? About how many hours did it take for the number of bacteria in the dish to double? Explain or show your reasoning. Use graphing technology to graph the function… Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Practice Problem 1: The population of a town is growing exponentially and can be modeled by the equation \(f(t) = 42 \boldcdot e^{(0.015t)}\). The population is measured in thousands, and time is measured in years since 1950. What was the population of the town in 1950? What is the approximate percent increase in the population each… Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 2: The revenue of a technology company, in thousands of dollars, can be modeled with an exponential function whose starting value is $395,000 where time \(t\) is measured in years after 2010. Which function predicts exactly 1.2% of annual growth: \(R(t) = 395 \boldcdot e^{(0.012t)}\) or \(S(t) = 395 \boldcdot… Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 3: How are the functions \(f\) and \(g\) given by \(f(x) = (1.05)^x\) and \(g(x) = e^{0.05x}\) similar? How are they different? Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 4: A bond is worth $100 and grows in value by 4 percent each year. Explain why the value of the bond after \(t\) years is given by \(100 \boldcdot 1.04^t\). A second bond is worth $100 and grows in value by 2 percent each half year. Explain why the value of the bond after \(t\) years is given by \(100 \boldcdot… Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 5: The population of a country is growing exponentially, doubling every 50 years. What is the annual growth rate? Explain or show your reasoning. Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 6: Which expression has a greater value: \(\log_3 \frac13\) or \(\log_b \frac1b\)? Explain how you know. Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 7: The expression \(5 \boldcdot \left(\frac12\right)^d\) models the amount of a radioactive substance, in nanograms, in a sample over time in decades, \(d\). (1 nanogram is a billionth or \(1 \times 10^{\text-9}\) gram.) What do the 5 and the \(\frac12\) tell us in this situation? When will the sample have less than 0.5… Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 8: Select all true statements about the number \(e\). \(e\) is a rational number. \(e\) is approximately 2.718. \(e\) is an irrational number. \(e\) is between \(\pi\) and \(\sqrt2\) on the number line. \(e\) is exactly 2.718. Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.
